Duration::numel¶

Back to Duration API Reference

Signature¶

std::int64_t Duration::numel() const

What It Tells You¶

numel() returns the number of logical duration lanes. It is the product of all extents reported by sizes(); a scalar is the rank-zero case and contains one lane.

The count includes NaT lanes because NaT occupies a position. It says nothing about validity, sign, or uniqueness. A shape with any zero extent has zero lanes but remains defined and retains its full rank.

Returns¶

The logical element count as std::int64_t. The query is constant time and does not materialize or scan duration values.

Examples¶

Example 1. Scalar, vector, and matrix cardinalities.

std::cout << pluss::duration::seconds(90).numel() << "\n"
          << pluss::duration::minutes({15,30,45}).numel() << "\n"
          << pluss::duration::hours({1,2,3,4}, {2,2}).numel() << "\n";

Output¶

1
3
4

Example 2. Equal cardinality does not imply equal shape.

const auto vector = pluss::duration::nanos({1,2,3,4});
const auto cube = pluss::duration::nanos({1,2,3,4}, {2,1,2});
std::cout << "vector dim=" << vector.dim() << " numel=" << vector.numel() << "\n"
          << "cube dim=" << cube.dim() << " numel=" << cube.numel() << "\n";

Output¶

vector dim=1 numel=4
cube dim=3 numel=4

Example 3. One zero extent makes the product zero.

const auto empty = pluss::duration::zeros({2,0,3});
std::cout << std::boolalpha << "defined=" << empty.defined()
          << " dim=" << empty.dim() << " numel=" << empty.numel() << "\n";

Output¶

defined=true dim=3 numel=0

See Also¶

  • dim: count axes rather than lanes.

  • sizes: inspect the factors producing this count.

  • isnat: count or select invalid lanes through a boolean mask.
